[Last time](../webgpu-two-holes-in-a-wall/) a wave went through a hole in a wall and made a
pattern on the far wall. A single slit made a broad hump. Two slits made fringes. It
looked as if each hole had its own pattern and each one needed working out.

They are all one rule. The pattern a long way behind a hole is the _Fourier transform_ of
the hole. A Fourier transform takes a picture and says how much of each ripple it is made
of: a few broad ripples and a few fine ones, in every direction. A hole is a picture too,
open where the wave gets through and shut where it does not. The wave leaves the hole in
all directions and each direction sees a different ripple of the hole.

The picture has changed from last time. Then we looked down on the tank from above and the
wall was a line with gaps in it. Now we look at the wall head-on, as a wave coming towards
us would see it. The wall is a flat sheet and the hole is a shape cut out of it. The slits
are tall bars and the pattern falls on a flat screen a long way behind, so it spreads in two
directions and not one.

On the left below is the hole in the wall, white where it is open. On the right is the
pattern on the screen, brightest in the middle. **Paint on the hole with the mouse** and
the pattern follows.

Each point in the pattern stands for one ripple. Where it is says how many crests of the
ripple fit across the hole and which way they run. How bright it is says how well the hole
lines up with the ripple. **Move the mouse over the pattern** and the ripple for that
point sweeps across the hole, red for the crests and blue for the troughs. At a bright point
the crests reach every open part of the hole together, so the open parts flash red and
blue in step and the sum swings far. At a dark point some open parts are on crests while
others are on troughs, they cancel and the sum stays near zero.

Try these:

- _Two slits._ The same fringes as last time, now with the rest of the pattern. The slits
  are tall and narrow, so the pattern is spread sideways and squeezed up and down. Move the
  mouse to a bright fringe and both slits flash red and blue together. Move it to the dark
  gap between and one slit is red while the other is blue.
- _Paint over half of one slit,_ or make a slit fatter. Whatever gets bigger in the hole
  gets smaller in the pattern. A wide hole makes a tight pattern and a narrow one a broad
  pattern.
- _Circle._ A round hole makes rings. It is how a telescope blurs a star.
- _Grating._ Five slits instead of two. The fringes get sharper.
- _Blank,_ then draw anything you like.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
viewof shape = {
  const ui = await import(new URL("../lib/ui.js", document.baseURI).href);
  return ui.segmented({
    label: "Hole",
    options: [
      ["one", "One slit"],
      ["two", "Two slits"],
      ["grating", "Grating"],
      ["circle", "Circle"],
      ["blank", "Blank"],

    value: "two",
  });
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| column: screen-inset
//| code-fold: true
//| code-summary: "Show code"
{
  // Shared WebGPU boilerplate: setup, buffers and the animation loop (lib/gpu.js), and
  // the fast Fourier transform (lib/fft.js)
  const gpu = await import(new URL("../lib/gpu.js", document.baseURI).href);
  const fft = await import(new URL("../lib/fft.js", document.baseURI).href);
  const ui = await import(new URL("../lib/ui.js", document.baseURI).href);

  // Controls are read live from their elements, so moving them does not restart
  // this cell.
  const shapeInput = viewof shape;
  const brush = 6; // radius of the brush, in cells

  // The hole on the left and the pattern on the right, each 512 by 512 cells
  const N = 512;
  const { canvas, device, context, format } = await gpu.setup({
    width: 1024,
    height: 512,
    resolution: "auto",
  });
  canvas.style.touchAction = "none";

  // The hole: 1 where it is open and 0 where it is wall, kept here and copied across
  const mask = new Float32Array(N * N);
  let area = 0; // how much of it is open
  let painted = false; // true once the shape has been changed by hand
  let dirty = true; // the hole has changed since the pattern was made
  let needRipple = true; // the ripple shown on the hole has to be worked out again

  // The slits are tall bars, 80 cells high, with their widths and spacings in cells
  const slitHeight = 80;
  const slits = {
    one: { width: 12, centres: [0] },
    two: { width: 8, centres: [-24, 24] },
    grating: { width: 6, centres: [-64, -32, 0, 32, 64] },
  };

  function shapeMask(kind) {
    mask.fill(0);
    if (kind === "circle") {
      for (let y = 0; y < N; y++) {
        for (let x = 0; x < N; x++) {
          if ((x - N / 2) ** 2 + (y - N / 2) ** 2 < 40 ** 2) mask[y * N + x] = 1;
        }
      }
    } else if (slits[kind]) {
      const { width, centres } = slits[kind];
      for (const c of centres) {
        for (let y = N / 2 - slitHeight / 2; y < N / 2 + slitHeight / 2; y++) {
          for (let x = N / 2 + c - width / 2; x < N / 2 + c + width / 2; x++) mask[y * N + x] = 1;
        }
      }
    }
    painted = false;
    dirty = true;
  }

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------- the transform
  const transform = fft.create(device, N);
  const maskBuffer = gpu.storageBuffer(device, mask);

  // Copy the hole into the transform's input: real part from the hole, imaginary zero
  const loadModule = device.createShaderModule({
    code: `
      @group(0) @binding(0) var<storage, read> hole: array<f32>;
      @group(0) @binding(1) var<storage, read_write> data: array<vec2f>;

      @compute @workgroup_size(16, 16)
      fn load(@builtin(global_invocation_id) id: vec3u) {
        if (id.x >= ${N}u || id.y >= ${N}u) { return; }
        let i = id.y * ${N}u + id.x;
        data[i] = vec2f(hole[i], 0.0);
      }
    `,
  });
  const loadPipeline = device.createComputePipeline({
    layout: "auto",
    compute: { module: loadModule, entryPoint: "load" },
  });
  const loadGroup = device.createBindGroup({
    layout: loadPipeline.getBindGroupLayout(0),
    entries: [
      { binding: 0, resource: { buffer: maskBuffer } },
      { binding: 1, resource: { buffer: transform.data } },
    ],
  });

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------- drawing
  const paramBuffer = device.createBuffer({
    size: 32,
    usage: GPUBufferUsage.UNIFORM | GPUBufferUsage.COPY_DST,
  });
  const cornerBuffer = gpu.unitSquare(device);
  const showModule = device.createShaderModule({
    code: `
      struct Params {
        area: f32,    // how much of the hole is open: the brightest the pattern can be is area squared
        kx: f32,      // the ripple picked out: how many fit across the hole sideways
        ky: f32,      // and up and down
        phase: f32,   // moves on with time, so that the ripple travels across the hole
        pickX: f32,   // where it is in the pattern, in cells
        pickY: f32,
        pad0: f32,
        pad1: f32,
      }

      @group(0) @binding(0) var<uniform> params: Params;
      @group(0) @binding(1) var<storage, read> hole: array<f32>;
      @group(0) @binding(2) var<storage, read> spectrum: array<vec2f>;

      struct Out {
        @builtin(position) position: vec4f,
        @location(0) uv: vec2f,
      }

      @vertex
      fn showVertex(@location(0) corner: vec2f) -> Out {
        return Out(
          vec4f(corner, 0.0, 1.0),
          vec2f(corner.x * 0.5 + 0.5, 0.5 - corner.y * 0.5),
        );
      }

      @fragment
      fn showFragment(in: Out) -> @location(0) vec4f {
        let n = ${N}u;
        let y = min(u32(in.uv.y * f32(n)), n - 1u);
        if (abs(in.uv.x - 0.5) < 0.0015) { return vec4f(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 1.0); }

        let crest = vec3f(1.0, 0.282, 0.204);   // #FF4834
        let trough = vec3f(0.22, 0.60, 0.85);

        // The hole, on the left, with the ripple picked out in the pattern laid over it:
        // red where its crests fall and blue where its troughs do. Where the hole is open
        // the ripple shows in full and elsewhere only faintly
        if (in.uv.x < 0.5) {
          let x = min(u32(in.uv.x * 2.0 * f32(n)), n - 1u);
          let open = hole[y * n + x];
          let ripple = cos(6.283185 * (params.kx * f32(x) + params.ky * f32(y)) / f32(n) + params.phase);
          let tint = select(trough, crest, ripple > 0.0);
          let shut = mix(vec3f(0.10), tint, 0.12 * abs(ripple));
          let through = mix(vec3f(0.92), tint, abs(ripple));
          return vec4f(mix(shut, through, open), 1.0);
        }

        // The pattern, on the right: the zero frequency is the first element of the
        // transform, so shift by half to put it in the middle
        let x = min(u32((in.uv.x - 0.5) * 2.0 * f32(n)), n - 1u);
        let f = spectrum[((y + n / 2u) % n) * n + (x + n / 2u) % n];
        let intensity = (f.x * f.x + f.y * f.y) / max(params.area * params.area, 1.0);
        // Four decades of brightness, on a log scale
        let t = clamp((log(intensity + 1e-9) / 2.302585 + 4.0) / 4.0, 0.0, 1.0);
        let dark = vec3f(0.10, 0.10, 0.10);
        let white = vec3f(1.0, 0.95, 0.9);
        var colour = select(mix(dark, crest, t / 0.6), mix(crest, white, (t - 0.6) / 0.4), t > 0.6);
        // A ring round the point whose ripple is shown on the left
        let away = length(vec2f(f32(x), f32(y)) + 0.5 - vec2f(params.pickX, params.pickY));
        if (abs(away - 8.0) < 1.5) { colour = vec3f(0.95); }
        return vec4f(colour, 1.0);
      }
    `,
  });
  const showPipeline = device.createRenderPipeline({
    layout: "auto",
    vertex: { module: showModule, entryPoint: "showVertex", buffers: [gpu.squareLayout] },
    fragment: { module: showModule, entryPoint: "showFragment", targets: [{ format }] },
    primitive: { topology: "triangle-list" },
  });
  const showGroup = device.createBindGroup({
    layout: showPipeline.getBindGroupLayout(0),
    entries: [
      { binding: 0, resource: { buffer: paramBuffer } },
      { binding: 1, resource: { buffer: maskBuffer } },
      { binding: 2, resource: { buffer: transform.data } },
    ],
  });

  // ------------------------------------------------------------- picking a ripple
  // A point in the pattern stands for one ripple: kx crests across the hole sideways and
  // ky up and down. How much of it the hole contains is the sum, over the open cells, of
  // exp(-2 pi i (kx x + ky y) / N). The transform on the GPU does this for every ripple at
  // once. Here it is done for just the one picked, to show it on the hole
  let pick = { kx: 11, ky: 0 }; // starts on the first bright fringe of the two slits
  let brightness = 0; // how much of the ripple the hole holds, relative to the most it could
  function updateRipple() {
    let re = 0;
    let im = 0;
    const w = (2 * Math.PI) / N;
    for (let y = 0; y < N; y++) {
      for (let x = 0; x < N; x++) {
        if (mask[y * N + x]) {
          const angle = w * (pick.kx * x + pick.ky * y);
          re += Math.cos(angle);
          im -= Math.sin(angle);
        }
      }
    }
    // The size of the sum is how bright the point is. As the ripple moves across the hole
    // the sum swings up and down by that much
    brightness = (re * re + im * im) / Math.max(area * area, 1);
    rippleReadout.textContent =
      `ripple: ${Math.abs(pick.kx)} across, ${Math.abs(pick.ky)} up · brightness ${brightness.toFixed(3)}`;
  }

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------ painting
  // Brush strokes go into the hole, on the left half of the canvas
  let painting = false;
  let last = null;
  const place = (event) => {
    const box = canvas.getBoundingClientRect();
    const fx = (event.clientX - box.left) / box.width;
    const fy = (event.clientY - box.top) / box.height;
    return [fx * 2 * N, fy * N];
  };
  function stamp(x, y) {
    const r = brush;
    for (let j = Math.max(0, Math.floor(y - r)); j <= Math.min(N - 1, Math.ceil(y + r)); j++) {
      for (let i = Math.max(0, Math.floor(x - r)); i <= Math.min(N - 1, Math.ceil(x + r)); i++) {
        if ((i - x) ** 2 + (j - y) ** 2 <= r * r) mask[j * N + i] = 1;
      }
    }
    painted = true;
    dirty = true;
  }
  function stroke(from, to) {
    // Stamp along the way so that a fast drag leaves no gaps
    const steps = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(Math.hypot(to[0] - from[0], to[1] - from[1]) / 2));
    for (let s = 1; s <= steps; s++) {
      stamp(from[0] + ((to[0] - from[0]) * s) / steps, from[1] + ((to[1] - from[1]) * s) / steps);
    }
  }
  // Over the pattern: pick the ripple under the mouse
  function choose(at) {
    const kx = Math.min(N - 1, Math.floor(at[0] - N)) - N / 2;
    const ky = Math.min(N - 1, Math.max(0, Math.floor(at[1]))) - N / 2;
    if (kx !== pick.kx || ky !== pick.ky) {
      pick = { kx, ky };
      needRipple = true;
    }
  }
  canvas.addEventListener("pointerdown", (event) => {
    const at = place(event);
    if (at[0] >= N) return choose(at); // the pattern side is not paintable
    canvas.setPointerCapture(event.pointerId);
    painting = true;
    last = at;
    stamp(...at);
  });
  canvas.addEventListener("pointermove", (event) => {
    const at = place(event);
    if (painting) {
      stroke(last, at);
      last = at;
    } else if (at[0] >= N) {
      choose(at);
    }
  });
  const stop = () => (painting = false);
  canvas.addEventListener("pointerup", stop);
  canvas.addEventListener("pointercancel", stop);

  // -------------------------------------------------------------------- the charts
  // The middle row of the pattern (the zero frequency vertically) is the first row of
  // the transform
  const readback = gpu.readback(device, [{ buffer: transform.data, bytes: N * 8 }]);
  let row = []; // {k, I}: brightness along the middle row, relative to the centre
  let needRead = true;

  const [rowHost] = charts.children;
  const draw = ui.plotter(Plot);

  // What last time's formula gives for these slits: a hump from the width of each slit
  // times fringes from the spacing between them, with k the number of ripples that fit
  // across the 512 cells
  function formula() {
    const kind = shapeInput.value;
    if (painted || !(kind === "one" || kind === "two")) return [];
    const a = slits[kind].width;
    const d = kind === "two" ? slits[kind].centres[1] - slits[kind].centres[0] : 0;
    const rows = [];
    for (let k = -100; k <= 100; k += 0.5) {
      const alpha = (Math.PI * a * k) / N;
      const hump = alpha === 0 ? 1 : (Math.sin(alpha) / alpha) ** 2;
      rows.push({ k, I: hump * (d === 0 ? 1 : Math.cos((Math.PI * d * k) / N) ** 2) });
    }
    return rows;
  }

  function drawRow() {
    draw(rowHost, {
      height: 220,
      x: { label: "ripples across the hole (sideways in the pattern)", grid: true, domain: [-100, 100] },
      y: { label: "brightness (relative to the centre)", grid: true, domain: [0, 1.02] },
      marks: [
        Plot.line(row, { x: "k", y: "I", stroke: "#FF4834" }),
        Plot.line(formula(), {
          x: "k",
          y: "I",
          stroke: "currentColor",
          strokeOpacity: 0.7,
          strokeDasharray: "4 3",
        }),
      ],
    });
  }

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------- the picture
  const readout = ui.readout(); // how fast the GPU is
  const rippleReadout = ui.readout(); // which ripple is picked

  // How long a 512 by 512 transform takes on this GPU: a batch of them, timed, with the
  // first one thrown away. It overwrites the transform's data, so the pattern is made again
  // afterwards (the hole starts out marked as changed)
  async function benchmark() {
    const warm = device.createCommandEncoder();
    transform.encode(warm);
    device.queue.submit([warm.finish()]);
    await device.queue.onSubmittedWorkDone();
    const runs = 100;
    const encoder = device.createCommandEncoder();
    for (let r = 0; r < runs; r++) transform.encode(encoder);
    const start = performance.now();
    device.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
    await device.queue.onSubmittedWorkDone();
    return (performance.now() - start) / runs;
  }
  const ms = await benchmark();
  readout.textContent = `${N} by ${N} transform: ${ms.toFixed(2)} ms`;

  shapeMask(shapeInput.value);
  const on = (element, handler) => {
    element.addEventListener("input", handler);
    invalidation.then(() => element.removeEventListener("input", handler));
  };
  on(shapeInput, () => shapeMask(shapeInput.value));
  drawRow();

  function frame(ms) {
    const encoder = device.createCommandEncoder();
    let sample = false;
    if (dirty) {
      dirty = false;
      area = mask.reduce((sum, v) => sum + v, 0);
      device.queue.writeBuffer(maskBuffer, 0, mask);
      const load = encoder.beginComputePass();
      load.setPipeline(loadPipeline);
      load.setBindGroup(0, loadGroup);
      load.dispatchWorkgroups(N / 16, N / 16);
      load.end();
      transform.encode(encoder);
      needRead = true;
      needRipple = true;
    }
    if (needRipple) {
      needRipple = false;
      updateRipple();
    }
    // The ripple travels across the hole a little each frame
    const centre = N / 2 + 0.5;
    device.queue.writeBuffer(
      paramBuffer,
      0,
      new Float32Array([area, pick.kx, pick.ky, -ms / 400, pick.kx + centre, pick.ky + centre, 0, 0]),
    );
    if (needRead && !readback.pending) {
      readback.copy(encoder);
      needRead = false;
      sample = true;
    }

    const pass = gpu.beginRenderPass(encoder, context);
    pass.setPipeline(showPipeline);
    pass.setBindGroup(0, showGroup);
    pass.setVertexBuffer(0, cornerBuffer);
    pass.draw(6);
    pass.end();
    device.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);

    if (sample) {
      readback.read((buffer) => {
        const f = new Float32Array(buffer);
        const centre = f[0] ** 2 + f[1] ** 2 || 1;
        row = [];
        for (let k = -100; k <= 100; k++) {
          const i = (k + N) % N;
          row.push({ k, I: (f[2 * i] ** 2 + f[2 * i + 1] ** 2) / centre });
        }
        drawRow();
      });
    }
  }

  gpu.run(invalidation, device, frame);

  // The canvas with the controls laid over its corner
  yield ui.stage(canvas, [shapeInput, rippleReadout, readout]);
}
```

## Analysis

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| column: page
charts = {
  // An empty host; the simulation cell above draws into it as data arrives
  const ui = await import(new URL("../lib/ui.js", document.baseURI).href);
  return ui.chartHosts(["row"]);
}
```

The brightness along the middle row of the pattern, for the **One slit** and **Two slits**
holes. The solid line is what the transform gives and the dashed line is last time's
formula for the pattern behind a slit: a hump from the width of the slit and, for two,
fringes from the gap between them. They are the same thing. The formula was the Fourier
transform of a slit worked out by hand and here the computer has done it for every point
at once. It stops matching as soon as you paint on the hole.

## A sum of ripples

In 1822 Joseph Fourier published his book on how heat flows. In it was the claim that any
pattern along a line can be built by adding sine waves of different sizes. A picture is a
pattern along two lines at once, so it can be built from ripples: waves that run across it
in some direction with some number of crests.

To find how much of one ripple a hole contains you multiply the hole by the ripple, cell by
cell and add up. That sum is one point of the pattern:

$$F(k_x, k_y) = \sum_{x, y} h(x, y) \, e^{-2\pi i (k_x x + k_y y) / N}.$$

Here $h$ is 1 where the hole is open and 0 where it is wall. The exponential is the ripple,
with $k_x$ crests across the hole sideways and $k_y$ up and down and $N$ is 512. The
brightness of the point is $|F|^2$. It is the sum you watch when you point at the pattern.
Where the ripple puts a crest on every open part of the hole the terms all add and the sum
is large. Where it puts crests on some and troughs on others they cancel.

## How the computer does it

The page works out that sum by hand for the one ripple you point at, a loop over the open
cells of the hole. For the whole pattern it would need a sum for every ripple. The GPU
does that for all 262,144 of them at once by a shortcut. We'll find out how later.
The readout under the canvas is how long it takes on this machine, measured when the page
loaded.

The shader that draws the pattern squares each result to get a brightness and puts it on
a log scale, four factors of ten from the brightest to the dimmest, since the middle is
very much brighter than the edges. The transform puts the zero frequency in the corner of
the array and the drawing shifts it by half to the middle.

## Sources

- Fourier, J. (1822), _Théorie analytique de la chaleur_ (Paris: Firmin Didot).
- Adams, C. S. and Hughes, I. G. (2018), [_Optics f2f: From Fourier to Fresnel_](https://academic.oup.com/book/43688)
  (Oxford University Press), for the pattern behind a hole as a Fourier transform.
